thread:
maya: Heads-up — on the int4 bring-up for model-v3.4 we’re seeing a consistent MRR drop on the long-doc cohort. Not huge but sustained. Can we discuss an anchoring/fallthrough rule for this canary? :thinking:

 tanner: Can you paste the quick numbers? sample size and relative delta?

 maya: 10k requests in cohort A (control v3.3 fp16), 2.5k requests in cohort B (v3.4 int4). 90th-day MRR: control 0.372 -> variant 0.354 (relative -4.8%). Long-doc subset (>=2k tokens) drift is bigger: -6.4%. p-value ~0.02 but noisy.

 li: Out of curiosity — latency and tail changes?

 maya: latency nearly identical median, p95 up ~12ms (from 180ms -> 192ms) on int4 under certain batch sizes. Not dominant. The main worry is quality delta on long docs.

 samir: Two parts we should codify: (1) an anchoring rule for small-sample bias, (2) an auto-fallback threshold when delta exceeds the tolerance window for a sustained window.

 tanner: Agreed. Proposal sketch:
```
canary_config:
  min_requests: 2000        # require at least 2k requests before hard promote
  warmup_window: 3600      # seconds
  smoothing: ema_alpha: 0.2
  quality_metrics:
    - name: longdoc_mrr
      threshold_relative: -0.03   # abort if drop > 3% relative
      sustained_duration: 7200   # must persist for 2 hours
      min_effect_size: 0.01      # ignore tiny noisy diffs
  auto_fallback:
    enabled: true
    trigger_if:
      - metric: longdoc_mrr
        comparator: lte
        value: -0.03
        samples: 1000
        consecutive_windows: 3
    action: rollback_to_previous
```

 li: Two nitpicks: set min_requests per-slice (longdoc min_requests 500) and use bootstrap CI rather than single p-value for small slices. Also we should cap consecutive_windows so a transient spike doesn't trip it.

 maya: Good call. I’ll update to per-slice minima. For bootstrap, do we already have tooling in Optimize to run quick ci?

 samir: Yes — Optimize has quick-bootstrap endoint /eval/bootstrap that returns percentile CI for metric deltas. We should wire that into the canary check so the comparator uses the 95% CI lower bound.

 tanner: Operationally we also want a human-notify path. Deploy-bot can auto-rollback but only after auto_fallback + notify on-call and #eng-ml with tags. Example rule: auto-rollback if lower_bound_delta <= -3% and sustained for N windows; otherwise, escalate to on-call with sample dump.

 deploy-bot: [system] Proposed action: creating canary policy draft "anchored-fallthrough-v1" and scheduling gate test for next canary.

 li: Also flag for prompt sensitivity — long-doc regressions often show prompt truncation edgecases in quantized KV merge. Need sample pairs for the worst 200 requests and a quick diff-run through the evaluator.

 maya: Action items: 1) I’ll update canary_config with per-slice minima + bootstrap CI comparator. 2) Tanner to add auto-notify/rollback wiring with deploy-bot. 3) Li to run sample diff and annotate top 200 regressions. 4) Samir to add a guard in Optimize: require at least two independent metrics (mrr + accept_rate) to both cross thresholds before immediate rollback (reduce false positives).

 tanner: Sounds good. If we can agree, I’ll land a minimal policy and run a dry-canary tomorrow morning (UTC).

 maya: +1. Thanks — let’s keep the promotion gated until the anchored rule is in place.

 samir: Quick thought — include an entropy/response-length check as a cheap proxy for hallucination changes. If hallucination proxy rises > 2x baseline and MRR drops > 2%, force immediate rollback.

 li: noted. I’ll add bootstrap code snippet to the runner:
```
# pseudo
ci = bootstrap_delta(metric='longdoc_mrr', control='v3.3', variant='v3.4', n_resamples=2000)
if ci.lower <= -0.03:
  mark_flag()
```

 maya: Thanks everyone. I’ll attach the sample dump and the preliminary eval table in the canary ticket. :thumbsup:
